inputs.task:
You are one seat in a structured forecasting panel. You have exactly
one job, defined below. Obey these laws before any instruction in
your job text:

1. PACKET-ONLY FACTS. Every fact, stat, price, quote, or date you
   state must come from the context you were given. Anything else —
   memory, general knowledge, plausible inference stated as fact — is
   FABRICATION and fails the entire exam. If the packet does not
   contain something, write it under "could_not_read" and reason
   without it. Never fill a gap.
2. OUTPUT IS ONE JSON OBJECT, matching the shape your job text gives,
   and nothing else: no prose outside the JSON, no markdown fences.
3. Every claim carries a ref. A claim without a ref does not ship.
4. Your distribution is over the moneyline only: {"A": p, "B": 1-p},
   each in [0, 1], summing to 1.
5. You are being graded against settled ground truth you cannot see.
   There is no audience and no reward for confidence; a calibrated
   number with honest gaps beats a bold number built on air.

JOB: STYLES, Round 1 — POSITION.
Your read is the interaction, not the fighters separately: style
classifications, the stance pass (same-stance or southpaw/orthodox —
what that does to each fighter's favorite weapons), the weapon-on-habit
map (each fighter's signature weapons against the other's documented
habits and defensive liabilities), and the neutralization test: name
each fighter's primary path to victory, then judge from the packet
whether the other has demonstrated neutralizing that path. Grade the
fight that remains if the key strength is neutralized.

CONTEXT: {"card_slot": "Co-main event \u2014 women's flyweight, No. 4 vs No. 6; a rebooking of a UFC 330 bout Blanchfield withdrew from injured", "date": "2026-10-17", "lock_basis": "T-30min before the main card (8:00 PM ET start)", "name": "UFC Fight Night 291: Buckley vs. Malott (UFC Edmonton)", "rounds": 3, "venue": "Rogers Place, Edmonton, AB, Canada", "weight_class": "Women's Flyweight"} {"A": "Erin Blanchfield", "B": "Jasmine Jasudavicius"} {"fighters": {"A": {"finish_profile": "2 KO wins, 5 submission wins \u2014 all five submissions in the first two rounds (Covers); needed just two takedowns to choke Cortez, who had not been submitted in eight years", "physical": {"age": 27, "height": "5-4", "reach_in": 66, "stance": "Orthodox"}, "style_line": {"defensive_liability": "Returning from an injury layoff of about 11 months (last fought Nov 2025) and already withdrew from this exact matchup once \u2014 sharpness is the unknown the price must pay for", "pace_profile": "Front-loaded finisher: all five submission wins inside two rounds; six of her last 10 went to decision when the early finish did not come", "primary": "Pressure grappler \u2014 smothering ground game with a submission finisher's timing (Renzo Gracie Jiu-Jitsu)", "secondary": "High-volume pressure striking (5.24 SLpM) to force the grappling exchanges", "signature_weapons": ["Single-leg chains into back takes (Action Network: her best work chains to and from single-leg attacks)", "Rear-naked choke (Cortez finish)"], "style_adjusted_read": "Her rates are elite but they are eleven months old; the style-adjusted read discounts the whole line for the layoff rather than reading it flat \u2014 the discount, not the rates, is where this fight is priced"}, "technique_tendency": {"favorite_counters": "Could-Not-Read", "stance_record_vs_opposite": "Same-stance pairing (both orthodox) \u2014 mirrored read applies", "tendencies": ["Needs the fight on the ground early \u2014 her finishes live in rounds one and two (Covers)"]}}, "B": {"finish_profile": "2 KO wins, 4 submission wins; decisions in 11 of her last 15 fights", "physical": {"age": 37, "height": "5-7", "reach_in": 68, "stance": "Orthodox"}, "style_line": {"defensive_liability": "The one elite opponent on her recent run finished her in a round (Fiorot TKO); at 37, athletic decline is a standing tax", "pace_profile": "Grinds all three rounds; the division's control-time queen (45.4%)", "primary": "Control grappler \u2014 makes fights ugly, wins on takedowns, back control and time (Niagara Top Team)", "secondary": "Size and length for the division (5-7, 68-inch reach) used to smother smaller grapplers", "signature_weapons": ["Takedowns into back control \u2014 the exact sequence the Edmonton recap describes her winning this style of fight with (pre-fight profile: dogged, position-first grappling)"], "style_adjusted_read": "Her modest striking line (3.27 SLpM) is the design of a control grappler, not a weakness \u2014 the number that matters is 45.4% control share against a woman whose finishes need early grappling exchanges"}, "technique_tendency": {"favorite_counters": "Could-Not-Read", "stance_record_vs_opposite": "Same-stance pairing (both orthodox) \u2014 mirrored read applies", "tendencies": ["Takes the initiative and makes opponents defend rather than build their own grappling offense (the pattern her whole Edmonton run was scouted on)"]}}}}

Your brief names: who imposes their fight, who dictates location and
pace, the two or three technique collisions that decide this matchup,
and your neutralization verdict. Anything the packet's style or
technique sections mark Could-Not-Read goes under could_not_read —
do not reconstruct a fighter's tendencies from reputation. Close with
your moneyline distribution, driven by the interaction read: if the
neutralization holds, price the fight that remains, not the fighters'
résumés.

Return exactly:
{"seat": "STYLES", "round": 1, "status": "ok",
 "brief": "<your read>",
 "claims": [{"claim": "...", "ref": "..."}],
 "could_not_read": ["..."],
 "distribution": {"A": 0.0, "B": 0.0},
 "state_pull": null}
